skill.name: browser-fingerprint-audit
skill.description: Audit a browser fingerprint for internal contradictions with the liarjs CLI - canvas, WebGL, WebGL2, WebGPU, audio, 220 fonts, WebRTC and timezone probes, scored against the TLS/HTTP/ASN view of the same request. Use when asked to run a browser fingerprint test, see what a fingerprint looks like, check canvas or WebGL fingerprint stability, compare a spoofed profile against a real browser, or find out whether a browser profile is self-consistent.
skill.summary: Measure browser fingerprint coherence across JavaScript, graphics, locale, and network layers.
skill.author: liarjsdev

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, examples, or documentation headings. The audit confirms a privacy-sensitive request to the documented endpoint and a medium-risk CDP attachment path that can read an existing browser session.

remediation.issue: The network scan sends browser and connection telemetry to a default third-party endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent before network mode, make offline mode the default, and display the selected endpoint before scanning.

remediation.issue: CDP mode can drive an existing browser and read page state.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit confirmation flag, validate loopback or allowlisted endpoints, and state that page contents may be exposed to the scanner.

remediation.issue: The documented CLI uses a floating package version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the package to an audited version and verify its integrity before execution.

content.value_statement: Browser spoofing and automation can create contradictions across JavaScript, graphics, locale, and network signals. This skill runs liarjs checks and explains whether the profile is coherent, suspicious, or likely spoofed.
actual_capabilities: Runs liarjs scans against a throwaway Chrome, Chromium, or Edge profile.
Checks JavaScript, canvas, WebGL, WebGPU, audio, fonts, WebRTC, locale, and timezone signals.
Compares browser-reported identity with TLS, HTTP, ASN, and edge observations.
Reports weighted failures with check identifiers and a coherence score.
Supports offline scans, saved report output, custom endpoints, and explicit CDP attachment.
limitations: The score measures internal coherence, not a site's complete bot or fraud decision.
Network mode sends one browser request and connection fingerprint to the selected endpoint.
Headless, datacenter, and unusual environments can produce legitimate failures.
The skill does not repair spoofing, change browser settings, or guarantee detector evasion.

use_cases.title: Validate Automation Profiles
use_cases.description: Check whether a Playwright or Puppeteer environment exposes contradictory browser, graphics, locale, or automation signals.
use_cases.target_user: QA engineers and browser automation developers

use_cases.title: Investigate Fingerprint Mismatches
use_cases.description: Use failing check identifiers to understand why a browser profile looks inconsistent across JavaScript and network layers.

use_cases.title: Monitor Browser Baselines
use_cases.description: Save scan results and compare them over time to detect regressions after browser, host, proxy, or automation changes.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Offline Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an offline browser fingerprint audit using a throwaway profile. Summarize the score, failed checks, and the most important contradictions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: local JavaScript-layer review without network telemetry.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Failed Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this browser fingerprint and explain each failing check in plain language. Separate automation signals, platform signals, and environment-specific limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate a suspicious or unexpected scan.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Run two browser fingerprint scans and compare the results. Identify new failures, resolved failures, score changes, and likely environmental causes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate a browser or infrastructure change.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Controlled CDP Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the explicitly authorized browser at this local DevTools endpoint: [endpoint]. State the endpoint before attaching, report page-access implications, and summarize every failing check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: inspect an existing browser session with explicit authorization.

output_examples.input: Run an offline scan against a fresh headless Chrome profile.
output_examples.output: Score: 72, Suspicious. Failures include the automation flag and headless viewport checks. Network-only checks were skipped because offline mode was enabled.

output_examples.input: Explain a mismatch between browser timezone and network timezone.
output_examples.output: The browser reports Asia/Shanghai while the network location resolves to America/Los_Angeles. This is a cross-layer contradiction, but a datacenter or proxy location can make the result expected.

output_examples.input: Compare a new scan with a saved baseline after changing the browser image.
output: Three new failures appeared: GPU identity, font set, and codec support.
The change is consistent with a different container image or Chromium build.
Run the same profile in a controlled environment before treating the result as spoofing.

best_practices: Use a throwaway browser profile and keep the Chrome sandbox enabled.
Use offline mode unless network comparison is necessary and authorized.
Compare against a saved baseline when the host, proxy, or browser environment is unusual.
anti_patterns: Do not attach to a running browser without explicit owner authorization.
Do not treat a low score as proof that a site will block or challenge the browser.
Do not send sensitive page content or private endpoints to an untrusted scanner.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits consistency among browser APIs, graphics, fonts, locale, timezone, WebRTC, and selected network observations.

faq.question: Does it modify my browser?
faq.answer: The default scan launches a temporary profile. It does not modify the user's normal profile.

faq.question: Does the scan require network access?
faq.answer: No. Offline mode runs JavaScript-layer checks without an outbound request. Network comparison requires an endpoint.

faq.question: What does the score mean?
faq.answer: The score measures internal fingerprint coherence. It is not a complete assessment of reputation, account history, or site behavior.

faq.question: Can I scan an existing browser?
faq.answer: Yes, with an explicitly authorized Chrome DevTools endpoint. Attachment can open a tab and read page state.

faq.question: Why can a legitimate browser fail checks?
faq.answer: Headless mode, datacenter networks, proxies, container graphics, browser builds, and unusual host settings can create expected mismatches.
